title: Thalia and Letters of Arius
attributionNote: Attribution is traditional or disputed. The catalogue records the attribution as a claim in the tradition, not as a settled fact.
description: Arius's own account of his teaching, known only from quotations in opponents and from letters preserved in church histories. The Thalia survives in fragments; the letters to Eusebius of Nicomedia and to Alexander are the fullest surviving statements in his own voice.
availabilityNote: Catalogue record only. The surviving text is fragmentary and is quoted inside the works of Athanasius and Socrates Scholasticus, which are streamed here. A separate edition of the fragments has not been imported.
